name: Hard-constraint-first model reduction
decision_structure: A complex system admits many global explanations, but a small set of high-confidence local constraints can sharply reduce admissible models.
rule: When the local constraints are independently well established, lock them before optimizing the global explanation; when those constraints are uncertain or the model begins violating basic constraints, lower confidence and seek discriminating evidence before committing.
operational_actions: List constraints whose uncertainty is materially lower than the rest of the model.
Freeze only the constraints with independent support.
Generate candidate models under those constraints.
Actively inspect each candidate for violations of basic local constraints.
Delay commitment when key constraints depend on low-resolution or incomplete evidence.
boundary_conditions: The supposedly hard constraints must be independently reliable.
The target system must actually be constrained by comparable local rules.
Model elegance cannot override contradictory high-quality evidence.
failure_signals: A candidate requires ignoring a basic chemical/measurement constraint.
Key parameters are being chosen mainly to preserve global elegance.
Available data are too weak to discriminate among several precise models.
notes: Provisional until the alpha-helix and DNA episodes are upgraded with contemporaneous primary-source locators.
